title: Kernel Harmonizer: Autotune policy for heterogeneous GPUs and dynamic sequence-length phases
creator: Aisha Kline
description: Build and validate an online autotuning policy — the 'Kernel Harmonizer' — that picks kernels per-request using GPU architecture signals and phase-aware sequence-length clustering. The goal is lower p50/p95 latency, reduced cost-per-token, and robust tail behavior for mixed prefill/decode workloads without impacting model output quality.
background: We've observed suboptimal kernel choices for workloads that exhibit multimodal sequence-length distributions and run across heterogeneous GPU fleets (A100/RTX/MI250). Existing heuristics pick a single kernel per model or per batch-size, which misses phase transitions within long sessions and tails under mixed prefill/decode workloads. This ticket explores a lightweight, sample-efficient autotuner that operates at request-time and can be warmed via microbenchmarks.
goals: Design a bandit-based autotuner (contextual Thompson Sampling) that balances latency vs cost vs safety margin
Implement phase-aware seqlen clustering (online) to avoid noisy per-request decisions
Provide warmstart profiles via microprobe harness and lightweight per-arch fingerprints
Integrate rollout controls in Console for canary % and instant fallback
Ship telemetry and SLO regressions detection for automated rollback
acceptance_criteria: Autotuner integrates into runtime kernel decision path behind config flag kernel_harmonizer=true
End-to-end p95 latency improves by >=8% on mixed seqlen benchmark vs baseline heuristic on A100 fleet (internal perf suite)
No measurable model-output divergence introduced (BLEU/ROUGE or model-specific evals within existing eval harness thresholds)
Canary rollout mechanism in Console enables 10% / 50% / 100% promotion and automatic rollback on >10% p95 regression
Microprobe warmstart reduces exploration cost (measured as extra CPU/GPU microbench cycles) by >=60% during first 6 hours
experiment_plan: Phase 0: Offline analysis of seqlen histograms (last 90 days) and identification of 6 representative workload clusters
Phase 1: Implement probe API and microprobe harness (single-GPU microbench) with a synthetic prefill/decode set
Phase 2: Prototype contextual TS bandit in a shadow mode (no effect on live routing) for 2 weeks to collect reward signals
Phase 3: Enable minimal exploration in canary region (5% traffic) with kernel_harmonizer and monitoring
Phase 4: Promote and run A/B for 2 weeks, gather latency/cost/quality metrics, then full rollout if targets met
implementation_notes: Context vector = {arch_tag, batch_size, cached_kv_hits, seqlen_cluster_id, decode_phase_flag}
Rewards combine latency and normalized cost with a conservative safety penalty for any QoI regression
Use Thompson Sampling with hierarchical priors per-arch to share signal between similar GPUs
Keep decision latency budget <= 0.5ms — implement decision as in-process lookups with lightweight RNG
Fallback policy: if no confident policy or telemetry anomaly, route to stable kernel specified in model manifest
Expose override config: exploration_rate, safety_margin_ms, warmstart_profile_url
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: exploration increases p95 tail — Mitigation: strict canary limits and automatic rollback triggers
Risk: noisy rewards from variable downstream network — Mitigation: use per-node normalization and control groups
Risk: degredation in output quality — Mitigation: pair every exploratory kernel with model-output checksum snapshots and thresholded gating
Risk: increased operational complexity — Mitigation: single flag toggle and Console rollout UI with clear metrics
rollout_plan: 1. Feature flag gated in runtime (default off)
2. Deploy microprobe + decision code to staging, run synthetic load for perf validation
3. Shadow run in us-east-1 for 2 weeks, evaluate telemetry
4. Canary 5% in us-east-1 with canary alerting on p95 and error-rate
5. Extend to 25% then 100% region by region after 2 successful canaries
notes: Design decision: prefer small, frequent microprobes over large disruptive experiments to limit cost impact
We evaluated contextual bandits vs. model-based RL; bandits won on sample efficiency and simpler safety reasoning
We'll reuse existing telemetry tags (kernel_id, decision_source, seqlen_bucket) to minimize schema churn
Prototype used A/B shadow traffic and showed 9.4% p95 improvement on internal 'assistant' workload with low extra cost
